u0: Nothing is outstanding: no client is waiting, no taken order is owed its food, no slipped food still needs retrieving, and the siren is silent. The shop is fully up to date, and the next siren, client arrival or food slip will open a fresh obligation. Waiting here is safe until something happens.
u1: The siren is ringing and has not been switched off, so the standing requirement is to reach the switch and toggle it. No client is waiting, no order is owed and no slipped food needs retrieving. Once the switch is toggled, the siren obligation is cleared and the shop is up to date again.
u10: A client is waiting with its order not yet taken, and food has just slipped. The pickup is immediate: food must be in hand on this step or the task fails. Afterwards the client's order still has to be taken, prepared and served.
u11: A client's order is untaken, the siren is ringing, and food has just slipped. Picking the food up on this step is mandatory; failing that fails the task. Taking and serving the order and silencing the siren still remain.
u12: An order has been taken but not yet served, and a client is waiting whose order has not been taken. Both must be dealt with: the waiting order taken, and prepared food eventually handed over for the outstanding order. The siren is silent and no slipped food needs retrieving.
u13: An order has been taken and not yet served, a client waits with its order untaken, and the siren is ringing. All three must be resolved: the untaken order taken, prepared food handed over for the taken order, and the siren switched off. The order of handling them is not fixed.
u14: An order is taken and unserved, a client's order is still untaken, and food has just slipped. The pickup is immediate and mandatory; if food is not in hand at the end of this step, the task fails. The untaken order and the outstanding serving remain to be completed afterwards.
u15: Four demands are open: a ringing siren, an untaken waiting order, a taken order still owed its food, and food that has just slipped. The pickup must happen on this step or the task fails. Afterwards the siren must be switched off, the untaken order taken, and the prepared food served.
u16: Food slipped from the agent's hands and was not held again on the very next step. That breaks the immediate-recovery requirement for good, so the task can no longer succeed. No later action can repair the failure.
u2: A client's order has been taken and the prepared food has not been handed over, so the client is still waiting. The remaining objective is to end up serving prepared food to that client, fetching and preparing it first if it is not already in hand. The siren is silent and no slipped food needs retrieving.
u3: Two obligations are open: the siren is ringing and a taken order still awaits its prepared food. The siren must be switched off and the waiting client must eventually be served; either task can be handled first. Clearing both returns the shop to an up-to-date condition.
u4: Food has just slipped out of the agent's hands, and the immediate requirement is to pick it up so that food is in hand on this very step. If this step ends without food in hand, the task is failed for good. No client or siren obligation is pending.
u5: Food has just slipped and must be picked up on this step, or the task fails. At the same time the siren is ringing and still has to be switched off. The pickup is immediate; the siren can be silenced once the food is recovered.
u6: A taken order still awaits its prepared food, and food has just slipped out of the agent's hands. The next step must be the pickup: food has to be in hand at the end of this step, or the task fails. After that recovery, the waiting client still has to be served.
u7: The siren is ringing, a taken order still awaits its food, and food has just slipped. Picking the food up on this step is mandatory; failing it fails the task. After the food is recovered, the agent must still switch the siren off and serve the waiting client.
u8: A client is at the counter and its order has not been taken yet. The order must be taken, and then food fetched, prepared and handed over to that client. The siren is silent, and no taken order or slipped food is pending.
u9: A client is waiting with an untaken order, and the siren is ringing. Both obligations are open: the order must be taken and its food eventually prepared and served, and the siren must be switched off. Either can be handled first.
